questions.stem: Based on the classification of RPGN with its etiological factor. Identify the wrong match:
questions.solutionHtml:
Type III - Lupus nephritis
  • Type III RPGN is typically associated with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis and is commonly seen in patients with small-vessel vasculitis, such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis (formerly known as Wegener's granulomatosis) and microscopic polyangiitis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 562

questions.stem: Which class of rapidly Progressive (Crescentic) Glomerulonephritis is associated with the presence of ANCA?
questions.solutionHtml:
Type III  (Pauci-Immune)
  • The class of rapidly Progressive (Crescentic) Glomerulonephritis that is associated with the presence of ANCA is Type III (Pauci-Immune).
  • ANCA is a marker for the presence of small vessel vasculitis (Wegener’s granulomatosis: C-ANCA and microscopic polyangiitis: P-ANCA)  and is commonly seen in pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis, which is characterized by the absence of immune complexes.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 562

questions.stem: All of the following are constituents of the crescent except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mesangial cells
  • Mesangial cells are not a constituent of crescents.
  • Crescents are cellular deposits that are composed of proliferating parietal cells, infiltrating monocytes or macrophages, and fibrin.
  • The crescents may obliterate the urinary space and compress the glomerular tuft.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 562

questions.stem: Rapidly Progressive (Crescentic) Glomerulonephritis with pauci-immune status is associated with:
questions.solutionHtml:
Wegener granulomatosis
  • Pauci immune type of RPGN may be a component of systemic vasculitis such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis -formerly called Wegener granulomatosis or microscopic polyangiitis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 562

questions.stemHtml: A 26-year-old patient presented with proteinuria, and hematuria. The PAS stain of renal biopsy is shown below. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
  • The given clinical scenario with a histological picture showing crescents is suggestive of Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN).
  • RPGN is a type of glomerulonephritis characterized by rapid deterioration of renal function, usually resulting in acute kidney injury.
  • The presence of crescents on renal biopsy is a hallmark feature of RPGN.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 562
